title: Make failures readable by someone who did not write it
problem: A failing check says that something went wrong, not what. To act on it, a reader has to see the trace, find the step the check points at, and distinguish a wrong tool from a loop from a denied unsafe attempt. Today only the author can do that, by reading raw JSON.
context: Final task of the pack. The viewer is static HTML generated from traces and check results with the standard library. This is where the evaluator becomes usable by someone investigating a failure, and where production readiness has something real to assess.
impact: An evaluation only its author can interpret does not change anyone's decision. This task is the difference.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A static HTML file generated from one trace shows every step with tool, arguments and result or error, and marks the step each failing check points at.
The view makes the competing explanations distinguishable: a wrong tool, budget exhaustion, a denied forbidden attempt and an unsafe completion each look different and are labeled.
Each scenario run prints a one-line summary with counts of successes, failures, budget exhaustions, forbidden attempts, correct refusals and unsafe completions.
A person with only the README can run the scenarios and open a failed trace in the viewer in under a minute.
The trace format and checks are documented as a stable contract, and an operations note covers a non-terminating policy, an unknown tool and a denied forbidden attempt.
Someone other than the learner opens a failed trace in the viewer and explains which step failed and why, using only the README and the view. The result is recorded, including where they hesitated.
Automated tests check that the generated view marks the failing step for each failure kind and escapes trace content safely, and pass at the submitted revision.
The learner explains how the view separates the competing explanations for a failure, one rejected layout, and what breaks first when traces reach hundreds of steps.

constraints: Standard library plus a test runner only. No web framework and no JavaScript dependency.
No network access and no model API. Every input is synthetic and generated or checked in by the learner.
AC-outside-check requires a real person. A simulated or model-performed walkthrough does not satisfy it, and recording one as satisfied is fabricated evidence.
Do not push to a remote, publish a package or deploy anything as part of this task.

scope.description: Readability and operability of the evaluator, not a new check.

investigation_areas: What a reader needs to see first to find the failing step
How trace content is rendered without letting it inject markup into the page
Where a first-time reader actually gets stuck, discovered by watching one
testing_expectations: Run the project's own test suite. State the exact command in the design; the learner chooses the runner and the layout.
Perform the quickstart on a clean clone before claiming AC-quickstart.
documentation_requirements: README quickstart, trace format contract and the operations note.
Record the outside walkthrough result verbatim, including where the person hesitated.
